$\underline{\mathbb C}$ supply the homotopy
\begin{equation}\label{local-curve-Thom-product}
(u_{\underline{\mathbb C}}^{KU})^\vee
u_{\underline{\mathbb C}}^{KU}
\simeq u_{\underline{\mathbb C}}^{KU}
 (1-\underline{\mathbb C})\simeq0.
\end{equation}
After applying the projection formula and the
polarization of $\operatorname{Ad}$, this homotopy induces the isomorphism
$\chi_z^{-1}:O_U(z)\to O(8z)$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
This is a direct calculation.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{local-curve-Shi-characterization}
Under \eqref{local-curve-theta-definition}, Shi's orientation satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{local-curve-Shi-value}
\theta_z(o_{\rm Shi}(z))
=\chi_z(o_{\mathbb C}(8z))\otimes o_{\mathbb C}(M_z).
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Let $\beta\in\widetilde K^0(S^6)$ have Thom image $x$.  Then
$\beta^\vee=-\beta$ and $\beta^2=0$.  For the class $k\beta$ occurring
here, the class $\mathcal V^{\rm top}$ in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{canonical-Shi-orientation} is therefore zero.  

By Lemma~\ref{local-curve-Koszul-comparison}, the orientation of the first
factor in \eqref{local-curve-adjoint-homotopy} is
$\chi_z(o_{\mathbb C}(8z))$. The orientation of the second factor, before
applying $d_z$, is $o_{\mathbb C}(-8z^\vee)$. Hence
\[
\theta_z^0(o_{\rm Shi}(z))
=\chi_z(o_{\mathbb C}(8z))\otimes o_{\mathbb C}(-8z).
\]
Here we have used \eqref{local-curve-duality-sign}. Applying $\rho_z$ gives
\eqref{local-curve-Shi-value}.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{local-curve-BSU-comparison}
Shi's orientation and the Joyce--Upmeier orientation agree on
$\operatorname{Map}_*(X_0^+,B\operatorname{SU})$.
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
On the component indexed by $z=kx$, Lemmas
\ref{local-curve-Thom-comparison} and
\ref{local-curve-Shi-characterization} give
$(\Phi_{\alpha_U(z)}\circ\theta_z)(o_{\rm Shi}(z))=+1$.
Lemma~\ref{local-curve-JU-characterization} gives the same equality for
$o_{\rm JU}(z)$.  Since $\Phi_{\alpha_U(z)}\circ\theta_z$ is an isomorphism
of torsors, the two elements are equal.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{family-canonical-orientations}
Suppose, in addition, that \(\pi:\mathfrak X\to V\) is relatively
Calabi--Yau and that
\[
H_c^3(X_v;\mathbb Z)=0
\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.
\]
Then the canonical Joyce--Upmeier orientations of the fibrewise components
on which \(c_2-c_1^2=0\) glue to a canonical trivialization of
\(
\left.O^{\not D}_{\mathcal C^{\rm cs}_{\mathfrak X/V}}
\right|_{\mathcal C^{\rm cs,\kappa=0}_{\mathfrak X/V}}.
\)
Via the relative comparison isomorphism, they also give a canonical
trivialization of \(O^\omega_{\mathcal M^{\rm cs}_{\mathfrak X/V}}\) over
\(
\Gamma_{\mathfrak X/V}^{-1}
\bigl(\mathcal C^{\rm cs,\kappa=0}_{\mathfrak X/V}\bigr)
\subset
\bigl(\mathcal M^{\rm cs}_{\mathfrak X/V}\bigr)^{\rm top}.
\)

If, in addition, \(H_c^4(X_v;\mathbb Z)=0\) for every \(v\in V\), then
\(\mathcal H^{4,{\rm cs}}_0(\mathfrak X/V)
=\mathcal H^4_{\rm cs}(\mathfrak X/V)\), and hence
\(\mathcal C^{\rm cs,\kappa=0}_{\mathfrak X/V}
=\mathcal C^{\rm cs}_{\mathfrak X/V}\).  In this case the two
trivializations above are defined on the whole relative spaces.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Consider the cohomology orientation
torsor \(L\) over \(\mathcal H^4_{\rm cs}(\mathfrak X/V)\), together with
a natural identification
\[
O^{\not D}_{\mathcal C^{\rm cs}_{\mathfrak X/V}}
\cong \kappa_{\mathfrak X/V}^*L.
\]
The restriction of \(L\) to the zero section has its canonical
trivialization.

For every \(v\in V\), the fibre of
\(\mathcal H^{4,{\rm cs}}_0(\mathfrak X/V)\) is path-connected by
definition, and
\[
\pi_1\!\left(
\operatorname{Map}_*(X_v^+,K(\mathbb Z,4))_0,0
\right)
\cong H_c^3(X_v;\mathbb Z)=0.
\]
Thus these fibres are simply connected.  The lemma below, applied to the
restriction of \(L\) to
\(\mathcal H^{4,{\rm cs}}_0(\mathfrak X/V)\), extends its canonical
trivialization along the zero section uniquely over that whole subbundle.
On each fibre this is the canonical zero-class orientation: both
trivializations extend the same canonical trivialization at the zero map,
and the extension is unique.
Pulling this trivialization back along \(\kappa_{\mathfrak X/V}\) proves the
topological assertion.  Pullback along \(\Gamma_{\mathfrak X/V}\), followed
by the relative comparison isomorphism, proves the algebraic assertion.

Finally, the components of
\(\operatorname{Map}_*(X_v^+,K(\mathbb Z,4))\) are indexed by
\(H_c^4(X_v;\mathbb Z)\).  Hence the additional vanishing of \(H_c^4\)
makes its zero component the entire mapping space, which proves the last
claim.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
Let \(q:Y\to U\) be a topologically locally trivial bundle whose fibres are
path-connected and simply connected, and suppose that \(q\) has a section
\(z:U\to Y\).  Let \(L\to Y\) be a principal \(\mathbb Z_2\)-bundle,
together with a specified trivialization of \(z^*L\).  Then \(L\) has a
unique trivialization extending the given trivialization along \(z\).
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
It is enough to work over one path component of \(U\).  The homotopy exact
sequence of \(q\), together with the section \(z\), shows that
\(q_*:\pi_1(Y,z(u))\to\pi_1(U,u)\) is an isomorphism with inverse \(z_*\).
Consequently, a double cover of \(Y\) is trivial if and only if its
restriction to \(z(U)\) is trivial.  This proves existence.  The ratio of
two extensions is a locally constant map \(Y\to\mathbb Z_2\).  Since the
fibres of \(q\) are connected and the ratio is trivial on \(z(U)\), it is
identically trivial.  This proves uniqueness.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
For a local curve \(X=\operatorname{Tot}_C(E)\), where \(C\) is compact and
\(E\) has complex rank \(3\), the Thom isomorphism gives
\[
H_c^i(X;\mathbb Z)\cong H^{i-6}(C;\mathbb Z).
\]
In particular, \(H_c^3(X;\mathbb Z)=H_c^4(X;\mathbb Z)=0\), so the theorem
applies to the whole relative compactly supported \(K\)-theory space for a
topologically locally trivial family of local curves.
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{nonorientable-geometric-calculation}
The bundle $F$ has rank two and $\det F\cong K_S^{-1}$. Moreover,
$D\in|2H|$, $K_W\cong\mathcal O_W(-3H)$, and
$K_Y\cong\mathcal O_Y(-2h)\otimes\varpi^*M$.
The morphism $\nu$ is the normalization of $D$, and its restriction to
$j(R)$ is $q:R\to S$, where $S\subset W$ is the section given by the
quotient onto $\mathcal O_S$. This section is the singular locus of $D$.
Locally near it, $\nu$ has the form
\[
D:\ v^2=zu^2,
\qquad
(t,\lambda,w)\longmapsto(z,u,v,w)=(t^2,\lambda,t\lambda,w).
\]
If $x_0\in H^0(W,\mathcal O_W(H))$ is induced by
$\mathcal O_S\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_S\oplus F$, then $x_0$ is nowhere
zero on $S$, and $B=D\cap V(x_0)$ is smooth and isomorphic to $R$.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Follows by a direct calculation.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
The variety $X$ is a smooth non-compact quasi-projective Calabi--Yau
$4$-fold.
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Where $x_0\ne0$, the derivative in the $\tau$ direction is nonzero.
Where $x_0=0$, the point lies over $B$, along which the differential of $d$
is nonzero. Thus $X$ is
smooth. Since $K_Z\cong p^*\mathcal O_W(-2H)$, adjunction gives
$K_X\cong\mathcal O_X$. The projection identifies $X\setminus V(p^*x_0)$ with
$W\setminus V(x_0)$; its complement has dimension three, so $X$ is
connected. Finally, for every $b\in B$, the whole fibre
$p^{-1}(b)\cong\mathbb A^1$ is a closed subvariety of $X$. Hence $X$ is
not proper.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{nonorientable-self-intersection}
There is a class $e\in H^2(Y;\mathbb Z_2)$ such that, for every
$s\in H^*(Y;\mathbb Z_2)$,
\[
f^*f_!(s)=e\smile s+j_!\bigl(\sigma^*j^*s\bigr).
\]
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
The fibre product $Y\times_XY$ is the reduced union of the diagonal and
the graph of $\sigma$ on $R$. This follows by a direct calculation in the
local model above; at a branch point its ideal is
\[
\bigl((t-t')\lambda,(t-t')(t+t')\bigr)
=(t-t')\cap(\lambda,t+t').
\]
The two components meet along the fixed curve of $\sigma$. Consequently,
their fourth homology groups give a direct sum decomposition of
$H_4(Y\times_XY;\mathbb Z_2)$. The refined pullback along the diagonal of
$X$ has multiplicity one on the graph, while its diagonal contribution
has the form $e\cap[Y]$. The pull--push formula gives the assertion.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{nonorientable-example}
There is an algebraic family $\mathcal F\in\operatorname{Perf}(X\times E)$
with proper support such that $[\mathcal F_t]=0$ in $K^0_{\rm c}(X)$ for every
$t\in E$, and a loop $\gamma:S^1\to E$ for which
\[
c_2(\mathcal F)/[\gamma]=-\alpha,
\qquad
\int_X\bar\alpha\smile\operatorname{Sq}_c^2(\bar\alpha)=1.
\]
The pullback of $O^\omega_{\mathcal M_X^{\rm cs}}$ along the resulting
loop is nontrivial.
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
The Steenrod--Thom formula gives
$\operatorname{Sq}_c^2(\bar\alpha)=f_!(\bar\beta\smile k)$:
the virtual normal bundle $f^*TX-TY$ has second Stiefel--Whitney class
$k$, while $\operatorname{Sq}^1(\bar\beta)=\bar\beta^2=0$ and
$\operatorname{Sq}^2(\bar\beta)=0$. The preceding lemma and the projection
formula therefore give
\[
\begin{split}
\int_X\bar\alpha\smile\operatorname{Sq}_c^2(\bar\alpha)
&=\int_Y\bar\beta\smile e\smile\bar\beta\smile k
  +\int_R\bar a_1\bar a_2\,\sigma^*j^*k\\
&=\int_R\bar a_1\bar a_2
  \bigl(\bar\Delta+\overline{c_1(Q)}\bigr)=1.
\end{split}
\]
Indeed, $j^*c_1(K_Y)=c_1(M)=\Delta-c_1(Q)$. The diagonal term is zero
because $a_1a_2$ restricts to $a^2=0$ on $\Delta$, and the remaining
term is $\int_R\bar a_1\bar a_2\bar b_1\bar b_2=1$.

Put $g=p_1\circ\varpi:Y\to E$, $\varrho=(f,g):Y\to X\times E$, and
$\mathcal E=\mathbf R\varrho_*\mathcal O_Y$. The morphism $\varrho$ is
finite and generically of degree one onto its image, which has codimension
two. Thus $\mathcal E$ is perfect with proper support, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$,
and the leading Chern class formula gives
$c_2(\mathcal E)=-\varrho_*[Y]$, also in cohomology with compact support.
Choose $\gamma$ representing the Poincar\'e dual of $a$ in $E$, with the
orientation for which
$c_2(\mathcal E)/[\gamma]=-f_!g^*a=-\alpha$.

Fix $t_0\in E$ and define
\[
\mathcal F=\mathcal E\oplus
\operatorname{pr}_X^*(\mathcal E_{t_0})[1].
\]
All fibres of $\mathcal E$ have the same class in $K^0_{\rm c}(X)$, since the
parameter curve is connected and the supports lie in the compact divisor
$D$. Hence $[\mathcal F_t]=0$, and in particular
$(c_1^2-c_2)(\mathcal F_t)=0$ in $H_c^4(X;\mathbb Z)$. Moreover,
$c_1(\mathcal F)=0$ and
$c_2(\mathcal F)=c_2(\mathcal E)-\operatorname{pr}_X^*c_2(\mathcal E_{t_0})$.
The second term has zero slant product with $[\gamma]$, proving the
asserted formula for $c_2(\mathcal F)$.

Finally, let $\ell:S^1\to(\mathcal M_X^{\rm cs})^{\rm top}$ be the loop
defined by $\mathcal F$ and $\gamma$. The comparison of
Subsections~\ref{compactly-supported-comparison}--\ref{KO-theoretic-interpretation}
and the factorization of
Proposition~\ref{BU-BSU-transition} identify its orientation monodromy with
that of the cohomology orientation functor along
$\kappa(\mathcal F)=c_2(\mathcal F)-c_1(\mathcal F)^2$.
By \cite[Theorem~3.2(c), equation~(3.22)]{JU}, this monodromy is
\[
(-1)^{\int_X\bar\alpha\smile\operatorname{Sq}_c^2(\bar\alpha)}=-1.
\]
Here the compactly supported formula follows from the compact one by
doubling a compact neighbourhood of the common support with smooth boundary
and extending the classes by zero. This proves that the orientation torsor 
is nontrivial.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{nonorientable-PT-orientability}
Let $X$ be a smooth quasi-projective Calabi--Yau $4$-fold, and let
$P=P_n(X,\beta)$ be the moduli space of PT-stable pairs with proper
one-dimensional support. For a loop $\gamma:S^1\to P^{\rm an}$, write
$\mathcal I_\gamma=[\mathcal O\to\mathcal F_\gamma]$ for the topological
restriction of the universal pair, and put
\[
\xi_\gamma=[\mathcal I_\gamma]-[\mathcal O]=-[\mathcal F_\gamma],
\qquad
\alpha_\gamma=
\bigl(c_2(\xi_\gamma)-c_1(\xi_\gamma)^2\bigr)/[S^1]
\in H_c^3(X;\mathbb Z).
\]
Then $\alpha_\gamma=0$. In particular,
\[
\int_X\bar\alpha_\gamma\smile
\operatorname{Sq}_c^2(\bar\alpha_\gamma)=0.
\]
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
We may replace $\gamma$ by a homotopic piecewise semialgebraic loop. Let
$Z_\gamma\subset X^{\rm an}\times S^1$ be the pullback of the universal
sheaf's support. Since this support is proper over $P$ and its fibres have
complex dimension one, $Z_\gamma$ is compact and semialgebraic of real
dimension at most three.

The manifold $T=X^{\rm an}\times S^1$ is oriented of real dimension nine.
Duality with supports therefore gives
\[
H^j_{Z_\gamma}(T;\mathbb Z)
\cong H_{9-j}(Z_\gamma;\mathbb Z)=0
\qquad(j<6).
\]
Here $H^j_{Z_\gamma}(T;\mathbb Z)=H^j(T,T\setminus Z_\gamma;\mathbb Z)$.
Outside $Z_\gamma$, the pair is canonically identified with $\mathcal O$,
so $\xi_\gamma$ belongs to $K^0_{Z_\gamma}(T)$. Its supported Chern classes
$c_1(\xi_\gamma)$ and $c_2(\xi_\gamma)$ therefore vanish, and hence vanish
also in compactly supported cohomology. Slanting
$c_2(\xi_\gamma)-c_1(\xi_\gamma)^2=0$ with $[S^1]$ gives
$\alpha_\gamma=0$, proving the assertion.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{PT-curve-neighbourhoods}
Let $C\subset X$ be a compact complex-analytic curve in a smooth complex
$4$-fold. Every neighbourhood of $C$ contains a relatively compact open
neighbourhood $U$ which deformation retracts onto $C$. In particular,
$H_c^j(U;\mathbb Z)=0$ for $j<6$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
Choose a locally finite triangulation of $X$ compatible with $C$. Since
$C$ is compact, open stars in sufficiently fine subdivisions give relatively
compact neighbourhoods which deformation retract onto $C$; see
\cite[Theorem~2.4 and Section~3]{TrivediTrotman2020}. Poincar\'e duality gives
\[
H_c^j(U;\mathbb Z)\cong H_{8-j}(U;\mathbb Z)
\cong H_{8-j}(C;\mathbb Z)=0
\qquad(j<6).\qedhere
\]
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
\label{PT-canonical-orientation-in-families}
Let $\pi:\mathfrak X\to B$ be a smooth, topologically locally trivial
complex-analytic family of $4$-folds, equipped with a relative Calabi--Yau
structure. Let $\mathcal P=\mathcal P(\mathfrak X/B)$ be the relative stack
of PT-stable pairs with proper one-dimensional support. Then
$O^\omega_{\mathcal P}$ has a canonical trivialization, compatible with
base change. On every fibre admitting a flag structure natural at zero,
this trivialization agrees with the induced Joyce--Upmeier orientation.
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
First consider a pair $\mathcal I=[\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal F]$ on a
single fibre $X$, and put $C=\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F$. Choose
$U\subset X$ as in Lemma~\ref{PT-curve-neighbourhoods}, with the restricted
Calabi--Yau structure. Since $H_c^3(U;\mathbb Z)=H_c^4(U;\mathbb Z)=0$,
the theorem of Section~\ref{sec:orientation-in-families}, applied over
a point, gives the canonical Joyce--Upmeier orientation on the whole
space $\mathcal C_U^{\rm cs}$. Apply it to
$\xi=-[\mathcal F]\in K_c^0(U)$. The Excision identifies its
orientation torsor on $U$ with the one on $X$.

We check independence of $U$. For an inclusion $U'\subset U$ between
neighbourhoods satisfying the cohomological vanishing above, extension
by zero induces
$\mathcal H^4_{\rm cs}(U')\to\mathcal H^4_{\rm cs}(U)$. The canonical
trivializations of the cohomology orientation torsors agree under this
map by excision. 
Now fix a pair over $b_0\in B$ and choose $U\subset X_{b_0}$ as above.
A local topological trivialization of $\mathfrak X/B$ extends $U$ to an
open subfamily $\mathfrak U\subset\mathfrak X|_V$ over an open
neighbourhood $V$ of $b_0$, with underlying topological family
$U\times V\to V$. Since $\mathfrak U$ is open in $\mathfrak X|_V$, it
is a complex-analytic family with the restricted Calabi--Yau structure.
Its fibres have vanishing third and fourth compactly supported cohomology.

Properness of the  support allows us to shrink a neighbourhood
of the chosen pair in a local analytic chart of $\mathcal P$ so that all
supports lie in $\mathfrak U$. Indeed, the image of the part of the
universal support outside $\mathfrak U$ is closed. The theorem of
Section~\ref{sec:orientation-in-families} applies to $\mathfrak U/V$.
Together with the excision, it therefore gives a
local relative orientation on $\mathcal P$.

At every pair, this local orientation agrees with the one already
constructed: choose a smaller neighbourhood of its support inside the
corresponding fibre of $\mathfrak U$ and apply independence of the
neighbourhood. Thus the local relative orientations agree on overlaps
and glue. The same argument gives independence of the local topological
trivializations, and naturality of the construction gives compatibility
with base change.

Finally, suppose that $X_b$ admits a flag structure natural at zero.
Its cohomology orientation, pulled back to $\mathcal H^4_{\rm cs}(U)$,
extends the prescribed trivialization at zero, and hence equals the
one used above. Proposition~\ref{canonical-orientation-at-zero-class}
therefore identifies the resulting orientation with the Joyce--Upmeier
orientation on PT pairs.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
Note that a non-proper complex-analytic manifold may have no smooth complex-analytic compactification, or, indeed, no embedding into a smooth proper complex-analytic manifold.

We shall thus construct the homotopy
without choosing a compactification and without explicitly using the Atiyah-Singer index
theorem.

Moreover, there is still no notion of complex-analytic Blanc's $K$-theory, so we cannot employ methods used above.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:analytic-comparison}
(a) Let $\pi:\mathfrak X\to U$ be a separated holomorphic submersion between
complex manifolds, and suppose that its underlying topological family is
locally trivial.  There is a natural homotopy making the square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=5.6em]
 (\mathcal M_{\mathfrak X/U}^{\rm cs})^{\rm top}
   \arrow[r,"\Gamma_{\mathfrak X/U}"]
   \arrow[d,"\pi_*^{\rm alg}"'] &
 \mathcal C_{\mathfrak X/U}^{\rm cs}
   \arrow[d,"\pi_!^{KU}"] \\
 U\times\operatorname{Perf}(\mathbb C)^{\rm top}
   \arrow[r,"\operatorname{id}_U\times\Gamma_{\operatorname{pt}}"'] &
 U\times KU
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commute.  

(b) The comparison maps respect direct sums, tensor products, and
duals.  The homotopy is compatible with composition, change of base, the
projection formula, and pushforward by a closed holomorphic embedding. 

(c) The homotopy carries a natural ``2-cell'' identifying relative analytic Serre
duality with the topological Serre duality of
Subsection~\ref{compstatement}.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:appendix-object-map}
For every exact functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, the square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=4.5em]
 \mathcal A^{\simeq}\arrow[r,"F"]
   \arrow[d,"\iota_{\mathcal A}"']&
 \mathcal B^{\simeq}\arrow[d,"\iota_{\mathcal B}"]\\
 K(\mathcal A)\arrow[r,"K(F)"']&K(\mathcal B)
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes naturally.  The resulting squares are compatible with composition,
natural equivalences between exact functors, and direct sums.
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
Observe that no detail in this section uses either a compactification (or
an embedding into a smooth compact complex manifold) or the resolution
property.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
\label{Levylocsyst}

Let us spell out what ``local'' means here.
If $\mathfrak V=\{V_i\}_{i\in I}$ is the chosen cover, put
$V_\alpha=\bigcap_{i\in\alpha}V_i$ whenever this intersection is nonempty.
An object consists of a finite complex $L^\bullet_\alpha$ of free
$\mathcal O_{V_\alpha}$-modules of finite rank for every such $\alpha$ and,
for $\beta\subset\alpha$, a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism
$L^\bullet_\beta|_{V_\alpha}\to L^\bullet_\alpha$.  These connecting
morphisms compose for $\gamma\subset\beta\subset\alpha$ and are the identity
for $\beta=\alpha$.  A morphism of local systems is a collection of
morphisms of complexes which commutes with the connecting morphisms. See
\cite[Definition~1.2, pp.~574--575]{Levy2008}.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
Let us also make explicit the two equivalences
in \eqref{eq:appendix-levy-models}.  Levy's \v Cech functor
$\check C:\operatorname{LocFfd}(q_X)\to
\operatorname{Perf}_{\rm an}(X)$ sends a local system $L^\bullet$ to the
total complex formed from the extensions by zero of the
$L^\bullet_\alpha$, with the ordinary \v Cech differential induced by its
connecting morphisms.  Its restriction to each $V_\alpha$ is
quasi-isomorphic to $L^\bullet_\alpha$; hence
\cite[Lemma~1.4 and Proposition~2.1]{Levy2008} show that $K(\check C)$ is
an equivalence.  

The other functor is Levy's natural embedding
$\jmath_X:\operatorname{LocCBun}_0(q_X)\to
\operatorname{LocFred}(q_X)$.  Using the chosen local trivializations, it
regards a bounded complex of continuous vector bundles of finite rank as a
continuous family of complexes of finite-dimensional Fr\'echet spaces,
which is uniformly Fredholm. $K(\jmath_X)$ is an equivalence by \cite[Lemma~3.5]{Levy2008}.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- proposition-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:appendix-topologization}
There are natural maps of spectra
\[
 \rho_X:K\bigl(\operatorname{LocCBun}(q_X)\bigr)\longrightarrow KU(X),
 \qquad
 \tau_X:K\bigl(\operatorname{LocFred}(q_X)\bigr)\longrightarrow KU(X),
\]
for which the diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=4.8em]
 K\bigl(\operatorname{LocFfd}(q_X)\bigr)
   \arrow[r,"K(KC)"]
   \arrow[dr,"\rho_X\circ K(\alpha_X)"'] &
 K\bigl(\operatorname{LocFred}(q_X)\bigr)
   \arrow[d,"\tau_X"] \\
 & KU(X)
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commutes up to a natural homotopy.  Under the first equivalence in
\eqref{eq:appendix-levy-models}, the common composite is the promised map
$\operatorname{cyc}_X:K(\operatorname{Perf}_{\rm an}(X))\to KU(X)$.
<!-- end proposition-20 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{CBun}(X)$ be the Waldhausen
category of bounded complexes of continuous vector bundles of finite rank
on $X$.  The inclusion
\[
 \operatorname{CBun}(X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{LocCBun}(q_X)
\]
induces an equivalence on $K$-theory: Levy proves that every local system is
quasi-isomorphic to a globally defined bundle complex
\cite[\S3.1, pp.~588--590, especially Lemma~3.2]{Levy2008}.


Levy writes the resulting map on homotopy groups as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-Q-plus-topologization}
 K_i\bigl(\operatorname{CBun}(X)\bigr)
 \longrightarrow K_i^Q(X)\longrightarrow K^i(X).
\end{equation}
Here $K_i^Q(X)=\pi_{i+1}BQ\operatorname{Vect}(X)$ is Quillen's
$K$-group of the exact category of continuous vector bundles.  The first
arrow in \eqref{eq:appendix-Q-plus-topologization} is the
Gillet--Waldhausen comparison.  For the second, the comparison of the
$Q$- and plus constructions identifies its source with the plus
construction on $GL(C(X))$ with the discrete topology; the identity
homomorphism to the same matrix group with the compact-open topology gives
the arrow to $K^i(X)$.  This is Levy's construction in
\cite[\S3, pp.~587--588, especially Lemma~3.1]{Levy2008}.  Applying the
construction at every stage of Waldhausen's $S_\bullet$ construction gives
the map of spectra $\rho_X$.

It remains to compare the bundle and Fredholm descriptions.  Levy's
Koszul construction gives the exact functor
$KC:\operatorname{LocFfd}(q_X)\to\operatorname{LocFred}(q_X)$ recalled
above.  Define $\tau_X$ by transporting $\rho_X$ through the equivalences
\[
 K\bigl(\operatorname{LocFred}(q_X)\bigr)
 \xleftarrow{\ \sim\ }
 K\bigl(\operatorname{LocCBun}_0(q_X)\bigr)
 \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
 K\bigl(\operatorname{LocCBun}(q_X)\bigr).
\]
The first is \cite[Lemma~3.5, pp.~594--595]{Levy2008}; the second forgets
the chosen local trivializations.  Levy's comparison of his two
constructions \cite[Proposition~3.6, pp.~594--595]{Levy2008} gives the
homotopy in the diagram.  Composing with
$K(\operatorname{LocFfd}(q_X))\simeq
K(\operatorname{Perf}_{\rm an}(X))$ gives $\operatorname{cyc}_X$.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:appendix-interval}
Let $\mathcal E$ be an exact category, and let $P$ be a finite compact
polyhedron.  An exact functor
$\mathcal E\to\operatorname{LocFred}(q_Y;P)$ to Levy's
Fredholm model over $Y\times P$ naturally determines a map
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-parameter-map}
 K(\mathcal E)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}\bigl(P_+,KU(Y)\bigr).
\end{equation}
For $P=[0,1]$, its endpoint restrictions form a homotopy between the maps
induced by the two exact functors obtained by restricting the family to
$t=0$ and $t=1$.
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proposition-21: body_md -->
\label{prop:appendix-compact-levy}
Waldhausen's $S_\bullet$-construction applied to this family, followed
by $T_N^{-1}$, determines a homotopy between the two maps
\[
 K\bigl(\operatorname{LocFfd}(q_X)\bigr)\longrightarrow KU(Y).
\]
<!-- end proposition-21 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:appendix-levy-canonicity}
After uniform quasi-isomorphisms have been inverted, the
space of Levy models for $(\mathcal D,P)$, with all comparisons required
to commute with the augmentations, is nonempty and contractible.  If a model has
already been chosen on some faces of $P$, or for part of $\mathcal D$,
the space of extensions is again nonempty and contractible.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proposition-22: body_md -->
\label{prop:appendix-proper-support}
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a holomorphic map of complex manifolds, and let
$Z\subset X$ be a closed analytic subset such that $f|_Z:Z\to Y$ is
proper.  Derived direct image defines an exact functor
$\mathbf Rf_*:\operatorname{Perf}_Z(X)\to
\operatorname{Perf}_{\rm an}(Y)$, and there is a canonical homotopy making
the square
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=5.4em]
 K\bigl(\operatorname{Perf}_Z(X)\bigr)
   \arrow[r,"K(\mathbf Rf_*)"]
   \arrow[d,"\operatorname{cyc}_{X,Z}"']&
 K\bigl(\operatorname{Perf}_{\rm an}(Y)\bigr)
   \arrow[d,"\operatorname{cyc}_Y"]\\
 KU_Z(X)\arrow[r,"f_!^{KU}"']&KU(Y)
\end{tikzcd}
\]
commute.  If $Z\subset Z'$ and $Z'$ is also proper over $Y$, the
restriction of the homotopy for $Z'$ to
$K(\operatorname{Perf}_Z(X))$ is canonically identified with the homotopy
for $Z$, with all higher compatibilities.
<!-- end proposition-22 -->
<!-- proposition-23: body_md -->
\label{prop:appendix-supported-serre}
For $E\in\operatorname{Perf}_Z(X)$, the adjoint of
\eqref{eq:appendix-supported-serre-pairing} is the equivalence
$s_{q,E}^{\rm an}$ in \eqref{eq:appendix-two-serre-maps}.  It is
independent of the analytic support chosen to contain
$\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal H^*(E)$ and is compatible with enlargement
of that support.
<!-- end proposition-23 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:appendix-cech-cousin-trace}
There are natural
$\mathcal O(V_0)$-linear pairings in the derived category
\[
 C_{V_0}^-(L^!)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O(V_0)}C_{V_0}^+(L)
 \longrightarrow\mathcal O(V_0).
\]
Its adjoint
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-cech-cousin-pairing}
 \rho_{V_0,E}:C_{V_0}^-(L^!)\longrightarrow
 \mathbf R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O(V_0)}
 \bigl(C_{V_0}^+(L),\mathcal O(V_0)\bigr)
\end{equation}
is a quasi-isomorphism and represents
$s_{q,E}^{\rm an}$.  After shrinking $V_0$, it is represented on bounded
finite free $\mathcal O(V_0)$-models by a continuous chain homotopy equivalence.
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
On a relative coordinate chart $p:U\to V_0$, an element 
$\eta\in\mathcal A_c(U/V_0,L^!)$ and a holomorphic section
$s\in\Gamma(U,L)$ are paired by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-local-cousin-pairing}
 \langle\eta,s\rangle_U=
 \operatorname{res}_{U/V_0}\bigl(\operatorname{ev}(\eta,s)\bigr).
\end{equation}
Here evaluation contracts the $L^!$ and $L$ factors and produces a class
in the relative Cousin complex for $\omega_q[d]$; in relative
coordinates $z_1,\ldots,z_d$, the normalization is
\[
 \operatorname{res}_0
 \frac{dz_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dz_d}{z_1\cdots z_d}=1.
\]
Thus \eqref{eq:appendix-local-cousin-pairing} is the local chain form of
the trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{q,Z}$ in
\eqref{eq:appendix-supported-serre-pairing}.

Suppose that $V_\beta\subset V_\alpha$, and let
$e_{\beta,\alpha}$ denote extension by zero of analytic functionals.
Cauchy's theorem gives
\[
 \langle e_{\beta,\alpha}\eta,s\rangle_{V_\alpha}
 =\langle\eta,s|_{V_\beta}\rangle_{V_\beta}.
\]
Hence the extension by zero maps in $C_{V_0}^-(L^!)$ are adjoint to the
restriction maps in $C_{V_0}^+(L)$.  Taking the \v Cech totals with the usual
graded signs gives the asserted derived pairing.
The formula for change of variables for the Grothendieck residue shows
that this pairing is independent of the relative coordinates.

Under the identifications of the two total complexes above, the resulting pairing
is the derived global sections of \eqref{eq:appendix-supported-serre-pairing}.
Its adjoint is therefore $s_{q,E}^{\rm an}$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:appendix-supported-serre}.
After shrinking $V_0$, choose bounded finite free models
$P\simeq C_{V_0}^+(L)$ and $Q\simeq C_{V_0}^-(L^!)$.
Cartan's theorem~B identifies the derived dual with
$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O(V_0)}(P,\mathcal O(V_0))$; compare
\cite[Lemmes~21--22, pp.~121--122]{RamisRuget1974}.
The adjoint is represented by a quasi-isomorphism $Q\to P^\vee$,
hence a chain homotopy equivalence.  Its maps and homotopies are holomorphic
matrices, so are continuous on sections.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- proposition-24: body_md -->
\label{prop:appendix-scaled-koszul-pairing}
One has a chain isomorphism and a trace map
that vary continuously for $0\leq t\leq1$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-koszul-self-duality}
 \kappa_t:K_t^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}
 (K_t\otimes\det(N))[-r],
 \qquad
 \epsilon_t:(K_t\otimes\det(N))[-r]\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{Y_U}.
\end{equation}
If $L$ is a finite locally free complex on $U$ and
$L^!=\mathcal Hom(L,\omega_{U/V_0}[d])$, there is a natural chain isomorphism
\begin{equation}\label{eq:appendix-scaled-local-duality}
 K_t\otimes\operatorname{pr}_U^*L^!
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \mathcal Hom_{Y_U}\!\left(
 K_t\otimes\operatorname{pr}_U^*L,
 \omega_{Y_U/V_0}[d+r]\right).
\end{equation}
At $t=0$ the auxiliary residue reduces to evaluation on $U$, giving
\eqref{eq:appendix-local-cousin-pairing} after the relative residue on $U/V_0$;
at $t=1$ it is the Koszul duality pairing for the Thom class of $j_1$.
<!-- end proposition-24 -->
